title: רגל הצפרדע שהמציאה את הסוללה
summary: Galvani's frog legs (Bologna, 1786: brass hooks on an iron railing; 1791 'animal electricity') vs Volta (two different metals, the frog is a detector); the lemon battery (zinc + copper ≈0.9 V, red LED ≈1.8 V so two lemons in series; zinc is the fuel, hydrogen on the copper; two zinc nails = 0 V); voltage adds in series but current does not; Volta's pile (letter to Banks 20 Mar 1800, 'artificial electric organ' after the torpedo ray; 84 × 0.9 ≈ 75.6 V ≈ a marbled ray's 70–80 V; Napoleon's medal 1801); Galvani's 1797 nerve–muscle contraction without metal and du Bois-Reymond's 1840s measurement — both were right; Eilat electric ray, 'galvanized', lithium batteries, the filling-and-foil battery; maths: series voltage, rounding up, mAh ÷ mA = hours.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (2 rounds) — nits left: the 1797 timeline icon (nerve on muscle) is abstract; gauge panel close to the canvas top on phones; Arto tip briefly covers the garden canvas on phones (template)
